No. 26S/F, Dda Janta Flats Pocket-2, Sector 7, Dwarka, Delhi. .....Claimant Versus 1. Suprasad Gayen S/o Sh. Bansidhar Gayen R/o H. No. 511, Gali no. 12/05, Valmiki Mohalla, Tughlakabad, New Delhi. ...R-1/ driver 2. Satyajeet Poddar R/o 51/1214, Dda Flats Kalkaji, Delhi. .....R-2/owner 3. Bajaj Allianz Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd. 1st Floor behind Weikfield It Park Viman Nagar, Pune. ....R-3/ insurance Company Date of accident : 11.07.2021 Date of filing of Dar : 21.12.2022 Mact No.: 920/2021 Rashmi Rana Vs. Suprasad Gayen & Ors. Page No. 1 of 30 Date of Decision : 12.07.2024 Rashmi Rana (Dar) vs Suprasad Gayen (237/21, Cr Park) on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183758126/ 1 Award 1. In this case, a Detailed Accident Report was filed by police on 21.12.2022 by IO ASI Sunder Pal which was registered as claim petition u/s 166 (4) MV Act qua injury to Ms. Rashmi Rana (hereinafter called the injured) in an accident allegedly caused by vehicle bearing registration number DL3SCY 3993 (hereinafter called the offending vehicle), driven by Suprasad Gayen (hereinafter called as Respondent no.1), owned by Satyajeet Poddar (hereinafter called R-2) and insured with Bajaj Allianz Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd. (hereinafter called R-3). 2. MACT No.: 920/2021 Rashmi Rana Vs. Suprasad Gayen & Ors. Rashmi Rana (Dar) vs Suprasad Gayen (237/21, Cr Park) on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183758126/ 2 Therefore, it MACT No.: 920/2021 Rashmi Rana Vs. Suprasad Gayen & Ors. He stated that he was employed as security guard at a nominal salary and also got severally injured in hospital. Rashmi Rana (Dar) vs Suprasad Gayen (237/21, Cr Park) on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183758126/ 3 5. In reply by R-3 Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company, it is admitted that the offending motorcycle was validly insured on the day of accident and was being driven by a driver without valid and effective driving license which is in violation of the policy and therefore, owner himself is responsible to pay any compensation to the injured. Issues: 6. From the pleadings of parties, following issues were framed by Ld. Predecessor of this Tribunal vide order dated 04.08.2022: i). Whether the injured suffered injury in a road traffic accident on 11.07.2021 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. DL 3SSCY 3993 being driven by R-1/ driver Suprasad Gayen owned by R-2/ Satyajeet Poddar and insured with R-3/ Bajaj Allianz Gen. Ins.Co. Ltd? OPP. ii). He deposed that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid and effective driving license on the date of accident which is violative of section 149(2)(a)(ii) of M.V. Act as insured/owner of the vehicle knew that the driver was not holding any license which makes him solely liable to pay the compensation to the deceased. Further, the surviving eye witness Rashmi Rana who was also injured in the accident was asked to appear for deposition and even an application was filed for her summoning, however, she did not appear apparantly on account of personal differences with family of deceased. He also argued that Rashmi Rana (Dar) vs Suprasad Gayen (237/21, Cr Park) on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183758126/ 4 Investigating Officer was examined in an attempt to fill that void. He also argued that non examination of an eye witness under certain circumstances cannot falsify the genuine claim of claimants. He relied upon following judgments: (i) Kashnumma Begum & Ors. Vs. The New India Assurance Co. Ltd & Ors. SLP (Civil) 1431v of 2000 (ii) NIC Vs. Pushpa Rana & Ors. (iii) Bharti Axa Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd Vs. Kavita & Ors. CM Appeal 108/2019 & MACT No.: 920/2021 Rashmi Rana Vs. Suprasad Gayen & Ors. 23. Another contention has been raised on behalf of R-1 that Rashmi Rana (Dar) vs Suprasad Gayen (237/21, Cr Park) on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183758126/ 8 MACT No.: 920/2021 Rashmi Rana Vs. Suprasad Gayen & Ors. Page No. 12 of 30 deceased Haider was not wearing a helmet at the time of accident which is why he sustained injuries. There is no record however, pertaining to that. Bare contention cannot take the place of proof. R-1 has not led any evidence as far as this aspect is concerned. It thus cannot be concluded that the deceased Haider was not wearing helmet at the time of accident. Further gravity of injuries sustained by Haider at the time of accident is on a different tangent against the aspect of negligent driving on the part of offending vehicle leading to the accident. 24. It is thus held that the accident happened due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle. Issue No.1 is decided in favour of claimant and against the respondents. ISSUE NO. 2 "Whether the petitioners are entitled to any compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?OPP" 25. Section 168 MV Act enjoins the Claim Tribunal to hold an enquiry into the claim to make an effort determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable. Same is reproduced hereunder for ready reference: "(1) Award of the Claims Tribunal.--On receipt of an application for compensation made under section 166, the Claims Tribunal shall, after giving notice of the application to the insurer and after giving the parties (including the insurer) an opportunity of being heard, hold an inquiry into the claim or, as the case may be, each of the claims and, subject to the provisions of section 162 may make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and specifying the person or MACT No.: 920/2021 Rashmi Rana Vs. Suprasad Gayen & Ors. Page No. 13 of 30 persons to whom compensation shall be paid and in making the award the Claims Tribunal shall specify the amount which shall be paid by the insurer or owner or driver of the vehicle involved in the accident or by all or any of them, as the case may be: Provided that where such application makes a claim for compensation under section 140 in respect of the death or permanent disablement of any person, such claim and any other claim (whether made in such application or otherwise) for compensation in respect of such death or permanent disablement shall be disposed of in accordance with Rashmi Rana (Dar) vs Suprasad Gayen (237/21, Cr Park) on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183758126/ 9 the provisions of Chapter X. (2) The Claims Tribunal shall arrange to deliver copies of the award to the parties concerned expeditiously and in any case within a period of fifteen days from the date of the award. (3) When an award is made under this section, the person who is required to pay any amount in terms of such award shall, within thirty days of the date of announcing the award by the Claims Tribunal, deposit the entire amount awarded in such manner as the Claims Tribunal may direct." 26. Before putting in frame the position of law, it is noted that the process of determining the compensation by the court is essentially a very difficult task and can never be an exact science. Perfect compensation is hardly possible, more so in claims of injury and disability. 27. The basic principle in assessing motor ve compensation claims, is to place the victim in as near a position as she or he was in before the accident, with other compensatory directions for loss of amenities and other payments. These general principles have been stated and reiterated in several decisions. [Support drawn from Govind Yadav v. New India Insurance Co. MACT No.: 920/2021 Rashmi Rana Vs. Suprasad Gayen & Ors. Page No. 14 of 30 Ltd., (2011) 10 SCC 683] . 28. This Tribunal has been tasked with determination of just compensation. "Statutory provisions clearly indicate that the compensation must be "just" and it cannot be a bonanza; not a source of profit but the same should not be a pittance. The courts and tribunals have a duty to weigh the various factors and quantify the amount of compensation, which should be just. What would be "just" compensation is a vexed question. There can be no golden rule applicable to all cases for measuring the value of human life or a limb. Measure of damages cannot be arrived at by precise mathematical calculations. It would depend upon the particular facts and circumstances, and attending peculiar or special features, if any. Every method or mode adopted for assessing compensation has to be considered in the background of "just" compensation which is the pivotal consideration . Though by use of the expression "which appears to it to be just", a wide discretion is vested in the Tribunal, the determination has to be rational, to be done by a Rashmi Rana (Dar) vs Suprasad Gayen (237/21, Cr Park) on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183758126/ 10 judicious approach and not the outcome of whims, wild guesses and arbitrariness.. ..." 29. Delineating the damages as pecuniary and non pecuniary, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in case of R. D. Hattangadi Vs. Pest Control (India) Pvt Ltd, 1995 AIR 755, made following observations: "9....while fixing an amount of compensation payable to a victim of an accident, the damages have to be assessed separately as pecuniary damages and special damages. Pecuniary damages are those which the victim has actually incurred and which are capable of being calculated in terms MACT No.: 920/2021 Rashmi Rana Vs. Suprasad Gayen & Ors. Page No. 15 of 30 of money; whereas non-pecuniary damages are those which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations. In order to appreciate two concepts pecuniary damages may include expenses incurred by the claimant: (i) medical attendance; (ii) loss of earning of profit up to the date of trial; (iii) other material loss. So far non- pecuniary damages are concerned, they may include (i) damages for mental and physical shock, pain and suffering, already suffered or likely to be suffered in future; (ii) damages to compensate for the loss of amenities of life which may include a variety of matters i.e. on account of injury the claimant may not be able to walk, run or sit; (iii) damages for the loss of expectation of life, i.e., on account of injury the normal longevity of the person concerned is shortened; (iv) inconvenience, hardship, discomfort, disappointment, frustration and mental stress in life." 30. Certain principles for delineating just compensation were enumerated in the case of Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr., (2011) 1 SCC 343, by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India. Following observations are relevant in the context: "40.General principles relating to compensation in injury cases 5. The provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the Rashmi Rana (Dar) vs Suprasad Gayen (237/21, Cr Park) on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183758126/ 11 nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which MACT No.: 920/2021 Rashmi Rana Vs. Suprasad Gayen & Ors. Page No . 16 of 30 he suffered as a result of such injury. This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned. [See C.K. Subramania Iyer v. T. Kunhikuttan Nair [(1969) 3 SCC 64 : AIR 1970 SC 376] , R.D. Hattangadi v. Pest Control (India) (P) Ltd. [(1995) 1 SCC 551 : 1995 SCC (Cri) 250] and Baker v. Willoughby [1970 AC 467 : (1970) 2 WLR 50 : (1969) 3 All ER 1528 (HL)] .] 6. The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Pecuniary damages (Special damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalisation, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising: (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. (iii) Future medical expenses. Non-pecuniary damages (General damages) (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries. (v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage). (vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity). In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i), (ii)(a) and (iv). It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii)(b), (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of MACT No.: 920/2021 Rashmi Rana Vs. Suprasad Gayen & Ors. Page No. 17 of 30 permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life. 7. Assessment of pecuniary damages under Item (i) and under Item (ii)(a) do not pose much difficulty as they involve reimbursement of actuals and are easily ascertainable from the evidence. Award under the head of future medical expenses--Item (iii)-- Rashmi Rana (Dar) vs Suprasad Gayen (237/21, Cr Park) on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183758126/ 12 depends upon specific medical evidence regarding need for further treatment and cost thereof. Assessment of non-pecuniary damages--Items (iv), (v) and (vi)--involves determination of lump sum amounts with reference to circumstances such as age, nature of injury/deprivation/ disability suffered by the claimant and the effect thereof on the future life of the claimant. 31. It is settled proposition of law as held in catena of judgments that "just compensation" should include all elements that would go to place the victim in as near a position as she or he was in, before the occurrence of the accident. Whilst no amount of money or other material compensation can erase the trauma, pain and suffering that a victim undergoes after a serious accident, (or replace the loss of a loved one), monetary compensation is the manner known to law, whereby society assures some measure of restitution to those who survive, and the victims who have to face their lives. 32. Record reflects that counsel for claimant Rashmi Rana was appearing however, nothing has been filed on record regarding income and avocation of the injured Rashmi Rana. Even injured Rashmi Rana did not turn up before witness box to show any loss of income as a result of accident suffered by her. MLC of injured filed on record mention the visible injury of injured to be swelling over right eye, bluish discoloration over left ankle and abrasion MACT No.: 920/2021 Rashmi Rana Vs. Suprasad Gayen & Ors. Page No. 18 of 30 over left ankle. There is also a mention that "Patient is absconding." During statement to the police, injured Rashmi Rana herself admitted that she left the hospital in panic when she came to know about the death of her friend Haider after informing his family about the accident which shows that she left the hospital her own without opinion of any doctor. She further never turn up to file any treatment record for medical bills or for claiming any loss of income. As such, it is considered that there is no loss of income suffered by the injured. 33. Having regard to the law as also discussed above regarding compensation, in the present case award amount is calculated as under: Sl. no. Pecuniary loss : - Quant 1. (i) Expenditure on treatment : There is no medical bill on record. However considering the nature of injury, it is presumed that injured must have spent at least Rs. 2,000/- on her treatment. (ii) Expenditure on Conveyance : No bill for conveyance has been filed, however, considering the nature of injury, it can be considered that claimant would not have Rashmi Rana (Dar) vs Suprasad Gayen (237/21, Cr Park) on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183758126/ 13 been in a position to use public transport. (iii) Expenditure on special diet : There is no prescription for special diet. By guess work, compensation can be awarded for special diet. (iv) Cost of nursing / attendant : The nature of injuries are simple. Even in the absence of documentary proof, compensation for attendant's charges is to be given for nursing services rendered by family members. (v) Loss of income : as discussed above MACT No.: 920/2021 Rashmi Rana Vs. Suprasad Gayen & Ors. Page No. 19 of 30 (vi) Cost of artificial limbs (if NA applicable) : (vii) Any other loss / expenditure : Not applicable 2 . Non-Pecuniary Loss : (I) Compensation of mental and physical shock : The nature of injuries are simple but mere fact that he met with an accident would have caused physical and mental distress. (ii) Pain and suffering : Compensation R for pain and suffering is to be awarded keeping in mind the nature of injuries suffered by the petitioner. (iii) Loss of amenities of life : (iv) Disfiguration : (v) Loss of marriage prospects : 3. Disability resulting in loss of earning capacity (I) Percentage of disability assessed and N/A nature of disability as permanent or temporary (ii) Loss of amenities or loss of Already granted expectation of life span on account of disability : The nature of injuries are grievous (iii) Percentage of loss of earning N/A capacity in relation to disability: As already discuss above. (iv) Loss of future Income: N/A (v) Future medical expenses Total Compensation R Deduction, if any Total Compensation after deduction R Interest
texts.facts: As per the investigation carried out by concerned police official, the information regarding present accident was received through GD entry no. 3A dated 11.07.2021 at 2.13 a.m. at C.R. Park Market No.1, Near Chauharaha with description "accident with injury, Mobile No. 7290030065" at PS Chitranjan Park, which was assigned to ASI Sundar Pal, upon which he rushed to the spot where he found one scooty bearing No. DL9SBZ 9348 TVS and motorcycle bearing No. DL3SCY 3993 Splendor in accidental condition and it was revealed that two riders on the scooty, one male and one female and motorcyclist have been rushed to the hospital in injured condition. DD No. 8A from AIIMS Trauma Center regarding MLC of patient Haider Khan, an unknown aged 30 years and Rashmi was received, whereby MLCs were collected. Patient Haider was declared dead vide MLC No.500278251, whereas patient Rashmi was not found in the hospital. No eye witness was found on the hospital. FIR under Section 279/337/304A IPC was registered. The accidental vehicles were got photographed and were seized. Any CCTV camera was not found functional near the spot and thus, any CCTV footage was not available. Page No. 2 of 30 On 12.07.2021, eye witness Rashmi came to the police station and made statement that in the intervening night of 10.11.2021 and 11.11.2021, she was pillion rider on scooty bearing No. DL9SBZ 9348 Jupiter registered in her name which was being driven by her friend Haider Khan while commuting from Dwarka to Tughlakabad at about 1.30 a.m. or 1.40 a.m. while passing through C.R. Park, Market No.1 crossing, a motorcycle in high speed, being driven negligently, suddenly came from the back from the right side impactfully hit the scooty on account of which scooty got dis-balanced and she alongwith Haider fell down on the road and sustained injuries. She also stated that Haider Khan lost consciousness and in the process motorcyclist also sustained injuries and that she noted down the registration number and make of motorcycle at the spot itself as she was conscious. She further stated that someone called the police and injured persons were taken to AIIMS Trauma Center. She also stated that she contacted sister of Haider Kahn informing her about the accident and after treatment, she had left for her place in a state of shock. Further investigation was carried out. Notice under Section 133 M. V. Act was given. Site plan was prepared at the instance of eye-witness Rashmi. Ownership details of offending vehicles were obtained. Notice was given to the owner Sh. Satyajeet Poddar. Offending motorcycle was seized. Original RC and Insurance of offending vehicles were taken into possession. Mechanical Inspection of accidental vehicles was got done. It was revealed by the registered owner of offending motorcycle that the same was being driven by one Suprasad at the time of accident, who was subsequently arrested and it was revealed that he did not have any valid and effective driving license on the day of accident. Insurance police was found to be valid. PCR caller Sh. Nitesh Tiwari as per the mobile number mentioned in the DD entry was contacted and his statement was recorded. Postmortem examination of Haider Kahn was conducted in which cause of death was opined to be "Blunt" injury MACT No.: 920/2021 Rashmi Rana Vs. Suprasad Gayen & Ors. Page No. 3 of 30 sustained to head, consistent with road traffic accident. Upon conclusion of investigation, IO filed charge sheet under Section 279/337/304A IPC & 3/181 MV Act against respondents. DAR was filed by Investigating Officer before this Tribunal. 3. R-1/Driver, R-2/Owner and R-3/Insurance company appeared before Tribunal. Copy of DAR was supplied. R-1 and R-2 were directed to show cause as to why security deposit atleast to the tune of Rs.19 Lakhs be not furnished by way of FDR for satisfying the award and also directed to file affidavit of income and assets. On subsequent dates, affidavit regarding income and assets of R-1 and R-2 were filed. Upon request, matter was referred to Mediation Cell for settlement. In the meanwhile, WS was filed on behalf of insurance company. Subsequently, reply was also filed on behalf of Driver (R-1). No reply was filed on behalf of Owner (R-2). Reply: 4. In reply filed by R-1, it is stated that R-1 was crossing Bipin Chanderpal Choraha, Market No.1, C.R. Park very carefully when scooty came in a rushed manner and collided with his motorcycle. It is further stated that he had made all efforts to avoid collision but it was scooty which was being driven very speedily and thus, the collision happened on account of negligence on the part of driver of scooty which also resulted in severe injuries to him. He specified that scooty driver just honked once but did not slow down. He also stated that there is no seizure memo of any Helmet worn by deceased at the time of accident to indicate that any Helmet was being worn by the deceased at the time of accident. He pointed out that the death of deceased happened on account of massive head trauma which establishes that the deceased was driving without wearing helmet whereas claimant had minor cuts and abrasion and was conscious. He also pointed out that claimant made no attempt to call for any medical or police help rather an onlooker telephoned the police. Page No. 4 of 30 was on account of willful negligence of claimant Rashmi Rana, on account of which timely treatment was not given and which led to death of Haider Khan. He also pointed out that claimant did not try to contact the police after accident till she received the notice under Section 133 M.V. Act and went absconding from the hospital. 7. Injured Rashmi Rana never turned up in the witness box. Any affidavit has also not been filed. However, it was requested by counsel for claimant that evidence led in connected case bearing MACT no. 921/2020 titled as Bano Begum Vs. Suprasad Gayen be also read in this case. An application was also filed by MACT No.: 920/2021 Rashmi Rana Vs. Suprasad Gayen & Ors. Page No. 5 of 30 counsel for petitioner in the connected matter to call her in witness box but still she did not come. 8. R-1 & 2 have not led any evidence. 9. R-3/Insurance company examined one Sh. Mukul Thakur, who tendered his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.R3W1/A and relied upon insurance policy alongwith terms and conditions Ex.R3W1/1 (colly). Counsel for R-3 argued that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid driving license on the date of accident which was in active knowledge of Tribunal/ Insured despite which he allowed/ entrusted the vehicle with that person and thus committed intentional breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy. It is argued that R-1 and R-2 are liable to pay the compensation and Insurance Company ought to be exonerated from any liability towards the claimant.
texts.arguments: Counsel for petitioner argued that R-1 was charge sheeted for rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle who has not led any evidence to controvert the allegations against him.
